reference: No GNU vec CLI exists. Contract expectations use the documented vec_doc API and direct arithmetic over the listed small inputs. Parity cases use independent Python 3 struct encoders/decoders for NumPy .npy v1 and BASHVEC2 file bytes; these Python branches run only under system Bash when type -t vec reports the builtin is absent. The candidate branch runs with the harness's empty PATH and never derives expected data from candidate output.
coverage: zero-initialized typed allocation, element access, type/length queries, reductions and predicates
indexed Bash-array import/export, copy and slice
mixed-width integer arithmetic, dot product and axpy
f64 reductions, scaling and checked conversion
empty-vector behavior and captured invalid-index status
NumPy .npy v1 import/export against independent struct encoders/decoders
BASHVEC2 save/load and byte-for-byte independent encoding
exclusions: No GNU command implements vec, so numeric API cases are documented-contract cases rather than GNU CLI parity.
Cross-endian and legacy BASHVEC1 files, malformed/truncated NPY inputs, non-finite floats, maximum allocation limits and broad randomized workloads are not included.
SIMD dispatch across explicit CPU feature sets is deferred because the runner supplies no CPU feature masking or alternate architecture.

cases.purpose: Check Bash builtin metadata for the registered loadable without invoking a vec operation.
Check the help builtin exposes the documented allocation, API and persistence descriptions.
cases.script:
doc=$(help vec)
[[ "$doc" == *"Typed dense numeric arrays"* ]]
[[ "$doc" == *"vec new -T TYPE -N LEN"* ]]
[[ "$doc" == *"BASHVEC2"* ]]
[[ "$doc" == *"vec import-npy PATH"* ]]
printf 'help describes typed vectors and persistence\n'
cases.stdout: help describes typed vectors and persistence

cases.purpose: Check zero initialization, signed element writes, type/length queries, scalar reductions and nonzero predicates on a small i64 vector.
cases.script:
vec new -T i64 -N 4 -h v
printf '%s\n' "$(vec get "$v" 0)" "$(vec len "$v")" "$(vec type "$v")"
vec set "$v" 1 -2
vec set "$v" 2 4
vec set "$v" 3 7
printf '%s\n' "$(vec sum "$v")" "$(vec mean "$v")" "$(vec min "$v")" "$(vec max "$v")"
printf '%s\n' "$(vec count-nonzero "$v")" "$(vec any "$v")" "$(vec all "$v")"
vec free "$v"

cases.purpose: Check dense indexed Bash-array import, independent copy, bounded slicing and export back to an indexed array.
cases.script:
source_values=(10 -3 8 0 5)
vec from-array -T i32 source_values -h source
vec copy "$source" -h copied
vec slice "$source" 1 3 -h part
vec to-array "$part" selected
printf '%s\n' "$(vec len "$copied")" "${#selected[@]}" "${selected[*]}" "$(vec get "$source" 1)"
vec free "$source"
vec free "$copied"
vec free "$part"

cases.purpose: Check small exact mixed-width integer dot, axpy, subtraction and addition results while preserving each destination vector's type.
cases.script:
x_values=(1 2 3)
y_values=(4 -1 2)
vec from-array -T i64 x_values -h x
vec from-array -T i32 y_values -h y
printf '%s\n' "$(vec dot "$x" "$y")"
vec axpy 2 "$x" "$y"
vec sub "$y" "$x"
vec to-array "$y" after_sub
printf '%s\n' "${after_sub[*]}"
vec add "$x" "$y"
vec to-array "$x" after_add
printf '%s\n' "${after_add[*]}" "$(vec sum "$x")"
vec free "$x"
vec free "$y"

cases.purpose: Check elementwise greater-than produces a u32 mask and where selects the corresponding values.
cases.script:
a_values=(2 7 0 -4)
b_values=(2 3 5 -4)
vec from-array -T i32 a_values -h a
vec from-array -T i32 b_values -h b
vec cmp "$a" "$b" gt -h mask
vec where "$mask" "$a" "$b" -h chosen
vec to-array "$mask" mask_values
vec to-array "$chosen" chosen_values
printf '%s\n' "$(vec type "$mask")" "${mask_values[*]}" "${chosen_values[*]}" "$(vec any "$mask")" "$(vec all "$mask")"
vec free "$a"
vec free "$b"
vec free "$mask"
vec free "$chosen"

cases.purpose: Check f64 parsing and reductions, then exact integral scaling and checked conversion to i32.
cases.script:
values=(1.5 2.5 -1.0)
vec from-array -T f64 values -h floats
printf '%s\n' "$(vec sum "$floats")" "$(vec mean "$floats")" "$(vec min "$floats")" "$(vec max "$floats")"
vec scale "$floats" 2
vec convert "$floats" -T i32 -h ints
vec to-array "$ints" scaled
printf '%s\n' "$(vec type "$ints")" "${scaled[*]}" "$(vec sum "$ints")"
vec free "$floats"
vec free "$ints"

cases.purpose: Check documented empty-vector reductions and capture an out-of-range get status without masking its diagnostic or stopping before state checks.
cases.script:
vec new -T u32 -N 0 -h empty
printf '%s\n' "$(vec len "$empty")" "$(vec sum "$empty")" "$(vec min "$empty")" "$(vec max "$empty")" "$(vec count-nonzero "$empty")" "$(vec any "$empty")" "$(vec all "$empty")"
if vec get "$empty" 0; then
  get_status=0
else
  get_status=$?
fi
printf 'invalid_get_status=%s len=%s\n' "$get_status" "$(vec len "$empty")"
vec free "$empty"

cases.purpose: Compare exported .npy bytes and vector metadata with an independent Python struct encoder for the NumPy 1.0 one-dimensional little-endian i32 representation.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t vec) == builtin ]]; then
  values=(3 -2 7)
  vec from-array -T i32 values -h v
  vec export-npy "$v" array.npy
  printf '%s\n' "$(vec type "$v")" "$(vec len "$v")" "$(vec sum "$v")"
  vec free "$v"
else
  python3 - <<'PYREF'
import struct
values = (3, -2, 7)
header = ("{'descr': '<i4', 'fortran_order': False, "
          f"'shape': ({len(values)},), }}").encode('ascii')
padding = (64 - ((10 + len(header) + 1) % 64)) % 64
header += b' ' * padding + b'\n'
encoded = (b'\x93NUMPY\x01\x00' + struct.pack('<H', len(header)) + header
           + struct.pack('<3i', *values))
with open('array.npy', 'wb') as output:
    output.write(encoded)
print('i32')
print(len(values))
print(sum(values))
PYREF
fi

cases.purpose: Import a small fixed NPY 1.0 fixture whose header and little-endian int32 payload are constructed independently with Bash printf; Python struct independently decodes the reference result.
cases.script:
header="{'descr': '<i4', 'fortran_order': False, 'shape': (3,), }"
{
  printf '%b' '\x93NUMPY\x01\x00\x76\x00'
  printf '%s%60s\n' "$header" ''
  printf '%b' '\x03\x00\x00\x00\xfe\xff\xff\xff\x07\x00\x00\x00'
} > oracle.npy
if [[ $(type -t vec) == builtin ]]; then
  vec import-npy oracle.npy -h v
  printf '%s\n' "$(vec type "$v")" "$(vec len "$v")" "$(vec get "$v" 0)" "$(vec get "$v" 1)" "$(vec get "$v" 2)" "$(vec sum "$v")"
  vec free "$v"
else
  python3 - <<'PYREF'
import struct
raw = open('oracle.npy', 'rb').read()
assert raw[:8] == b'\x93NUMPY\x01\x00'
header_length = struct.unpack('<H', raw[8:10])[0]
header = raw[10:10 + header_length].decode('ascii')
assert "'descr': '<i4'" in header
assert "'fortran_order': False" in header
assert "'shape': (3,)" in header
values = struct.unpack('<3i', raw[10 + header_length:])
print('i32')
print(len(values))
for value in values:
    print(value)
print(sum(values))
PYREF
fi

cases.purpose: Compare the BASHVEC2 save artifact with an independent Python struct encoder, then load it and check the documented type, length and values.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t vec) == builtin ]]; then
  values=(3 -2 7)
  vec from-array -T i32 values -h v
  vec save "$v" vector.bvec
  vec load vector.bvec -h loaded
  printf '%s\n' "$(vec type "$loaded")" "$(vec len "$loaded")" "$(vec get "$loaded" 0)" "$(vec get "$loaded" 1)" "$(vec get "$loaded" 2)" "$(vec sum "$loaded")"
  vec free "$v"
  vec free "$loaded"
else
  python3 - <<'PYREF'
import struct
import sys
values = (3, -2, 7)
order = '<' if sys.byteorder == 'little' else '>'
endian = 0 if sys.byteorder == 'little' else 1
encoded = (b'BASHVEC2' + bytes((2, endian))
           + struct.pack(order + 'I', 0)
           + struct.pack(order + 'Q', len(values))
           + struct.pack(order + '3i', *values))
with open('vector.bvec', 'wb') as output:
    output.write(encoded)
print('i32')
print(len(values))
for value in values:
    print(value)
print(sum(values))
PYREF
fi

cases.purpose: Exercise scalar/SSE2/AVX2 backend selection and reduction equivalence on explicitly controlled CPU feature sets.
cases.reason: Most of the matrix is reachable through the documented BASHVEC_BACKEND override on the existing VM. Masking AVX2 at runtime needs a VM CPU-model variant.

cases.purpose: Mutation of a copied vector leaves the original element unchanged.
cases.script:
values=(2 4 6)
vec from-array -T i32 values -h a
vec copy "$a" -h b
vec set "$b" 0 9
vec get "$a" 0
vec get "$b" 0
vec free "$a"
vec free "$b"
